inspiration.observed_pattern: A recursive CTE follows directed exchange edges with UNION DISTINCT, aggregates each discovered chain by ordinal grouping, deduplicates equal length/value pairs, and ranks the unique summaries with RANK().
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored warehouse transfer-cycle report. A recursive CTE follows fixed transfer edges from each origin, UNION DISTINCT terminates cyclic paths, grouped ordinal summaries collapse duplicate cycle totals, and RANK orders the unique length/value results. The source schema, participants, values, and gift-exchange context are newly authored.

fixture_notes: Transfer edges form one three-step cycle and two distinct two-step cycles with the same total, so grouped ordinal summaries retain one row for the repeated two-step total while RANK assigns deterministic ranks by length and value.
determinism_notes: Transfer IDs, participants, values, recursive joins, ordinal grouping, ranking keys, and final ordering are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE transfer_cycles (transfer_id INT PRIMARY KEY, sender_id INT NOT NULL, receiver_id INT NOT NULL, transfer_value INT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: WITH RECURSIVE transfer_paths (sender_id, receiver_id, transfer_value, start_id) AS (SELECT sender_id, receiver_id, transfer_value, sender_id FROM transfer_cycles UNION SELECT t.sender_id, t.receiver_id, t.transfer_value, p.start_id FROM transfer_cycles AS t INNER JOIN transfer_paths AS p ON t.sender_id = p.receiver_id AND t.sender_id <> p.start_id), cycle_totals AS (SELECT start_id, COUNT(*) AS chain_length, SUM(transfer_value) AS total_transfer_value FROM transfer_paths GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY NULL), unique_cycle_totals AS (SELECT chain_length, total_transfer_value FROM cycle_totals GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY NULL) SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY chain_length DESC, total_transfer_value DESC) AS cycle_rank, chain_length, total_transfer_value FROM unique_cycle_totals ORDER BY cycle_rank, chain_length DESC, total_transfer_value DESC

checks.sql: SELECT transfer_id, sender_id, receiver_id, transfer_value FROM transfer_cycles ORDER BY transfer_id
